objective_for_doctor: A 2-year-old M patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: jaw stiffness.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
Jaw stiffness. I also have annoying muscle spasms in my face, neck, or other parts of my body. I have suddenly had difficulty or an inability to open my mouth, with jaw pain when opening it.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—when did the jaw stiffness and pain start, and is it sudden (over hours) or gradual (over days)? Also, do the facial/neck spasms come with fever or any recent injury/illness?  
Doctor: Does your child have trouble swallowing, drooling, voice change, or stiffness that’s spreading to the rest of the body?  
Doctor: Any recent wound/cut, dental work, or possible exposure to contaminated soil—and has the child received the full tetanus vaccination series?

Doctor: I need to check for safety—right now, is your child drooling or having trouble swallowing, and can they open their mouth at all (even a little) or is it completely locked?  
Doctor: Also, do you see a fever, a painful swollen jaw/neck area, or any stiffening of the whole body/back that comes in spasms?

Doctor: I need to assess urgency—right now, is your child drooling or unable to swallow, and does any jaw opening happen (even 1–2 finger widths), or is it completely locked?  
Doctor: Also, do you see fever or a hot, swollen, very tender area near the jaw/neck, and is the back/neck becoming rigid or arching with spasms?

Doctor: I’ll examine them now—can you let me check mouth opening (how many fingers), look for drooling, and feel the jaw/neck for swelling or tenderness?  
Doctor: While I do that, I need one quick history: any fever, recent dental/ear/throat infection, or a new bite/skin wound in the last 2–4 weeks?

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—since you can’t answer history, I’ll focus on exam: can you confirm if the child can open the mouth at all (even 1–2 finger widths) and whether there’s drooling or trouble swallowing; I’m also checking for swollen/tender jaw or neck.  
Doctor: Next, I need one last key check—look for muscle stiffness/spasms triggered by light touch/sound and whether the child is fully vaccinated for tetanus (or any missing doses); if you truly don’t know, I’ll treat this as possibly serious.

Doctor: I can’t risk waiting—since history is unknown, I’m going to treat this as potentially **tetanus vs other life‑threatening jaw lock**. First, right now: is the child **drooling or unable to swallow**, and can they open the mouth **at least 1–2 finger widths**?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Tetanus risk assessment labs as available (CBC, CRP) and **vitals** now; REQUEST TEST: consider **CT/MRI only if stable** to rule out deep neck space infection.  
Doctor: I’m moving toward **tetanus (trismus with facial/neck spasms and inability to open mouth, especially if vaccination status is uncertain)** unless you confirm an alternative like fever with a swollen tender jaw/neck or clear dental/ear infection.  
DIAGNOSIS READY: Suspected neonatal/infantile tetanus (trismus with generalized muscle spasms; vaccination status unknown)
